title: 60th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The 60th sitting opened at 10:33 and the Speaker announced it as the last sitting of the session. Members allowed Kendhoo member Mauroof Zakir's urgent matter, about a verse of the Quran being altered in the state broadcaster's live coverage of the President's 8 December event in Raasdhoo, to be debated (70 yes, none against); debate was heated, with several points of order and a split between MDP members, who largely backed the motion, and PNC and allied members, who called it political or a technical fault. The House sent the President's nominees for the Broadcasting and Elections Commissions to the Independent Institutions Committee, read the first reading of the gang crimes bill, closed debate on the Vice President's Office Bill, and after a break from 11:55 to 13:01 began debating a Finance Committee report on the Foreign Ministry audit reports for 2010 to 2021. The text ends mid-speech in that debate, and the text layer is garbled in places so speaker gists are approximate. Members finished debating Finance Committee reports on audits of the Foreign Affairs and Higher Education ministries, then debated and passed the Foreign Currency Bill (tourism operators must convert part of their foreign income) after a heated exchange over what the bill does. They also passed a Finance Committee report on compensation the state paid to various parties, which sharply split government and opposition members. The Majlis then voted on each item, accepted the Vice President's Office Bill for committee review, confirmed a Maldives Inland Revenue Authority board nominee, and the chair closed the last sitting of the session. A few short exchanges are garbled in the source text. This part contains only the electronic voting record attached to the minutes, with no debate. It shows an open vote on a nominee named Shuaib for a Maldives Inland Revenue Authority Board member seat, recorded at 2:50 PM. 69 members voted yes, none voted no or abstained, and 4 members did not vote.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Called the matter sensitive and said altering Quranic verses must be condemned; urged investigating who did it.
Said the House should hold those responsible to account rather than cite past governments.
On the Finance Committee report, questioned the presenter's record of raising concerns about audit reports in committee.
Said the Finance Committee spent one 14-minute meeting on a ten-year audit report and called its presentation untrue.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said the altered verse is a fact; the question is whether it was accident, a technical fault or negligence, and cited loss of public trust.
Said the bill's 20 percent option was optional and criticised PNC members for going against the President's remarks.
Alleged a US$55 million payment to Noomadi followed false statements by the current President at arbitration.
Said the Majlis should look at the Noomadi settlement in the compensation report.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said the broadcaster would not act deliberately, condemned attacks on its staff, and called the motion political.
Thanked the Finance Committee for reviewing 12 years of Foreign Ministry audit reports.
Raised points of order on the debate, including that a remark was not a point of order.
Backed the Foreign Currency Bill report and hoped it would ease the dollar shortage and lower prices.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Said the live-feed jump was a technical issue examined by the broadcaster and called the urgent matter politically driven.
Backed the Finance Committee report and criticised spending at overseas missions.
Raised points of order that claims about which governments the audit years belonged to were inaccurate.
Raised a point that committee matters held in secret should not be revealed on the floor.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said MDP committee members did not refuse to review audits and that 12 years of reports cannot be done in a year.
Said many audited years fell under the previous PPM government and objected to being blamed.
Raised a point saying he has never worked as a consultant for any government body.
On the Foreign Currency Bill, said it could deter tourism investors and make foreign bank lending harder.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Raised the urgent matter: state media aired a Quranic verse with a word removed; asked the government to act under Article 192.
Said altering Quranic verses is unacceptable in an Islamic country and asked for those responsible to be identified and punished.
Objected by point of order to remarks saying members do not accept Islam or the Quran.

speakers.name: Ahmed Saleem
positions: Presented the Finance Committee report on the Foreign Ministry's audit reports for 2010 to 2021; about 1,500 reports are pending.
Raised points of order accusing a colleague of misstating how the committee works.
Presented the Finance Committee report on the Higher Education audits and discussed his own past service on the committee.
Presented the Foreign Currency Bill committee report and said the committee consulted affected parties and made changes.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: As the bill's sponsor, said the committee consulted tourism stakeholders and made changes, and that converting US$500 per guest at the bank rate is not seizure.
Raised several points of order, objecting to how the podium was used and to remarks about the President.
Said the 20 percent versus US$500 comparison made by opponents was misleading.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Raised a point of order that members should not address the chair in English, but by the title.
Said state TV is funded by the public yet gives the opposition no space, and asked for equal opportunities.
Said the bill does not define gross sales proceeds, that taxes and service charge should not count, and asked for clearer wording.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Criticised the mover, citing the MDP government's record on religion, including a report by the MDN group.
Said the mover's concern was political, drawing on MDP-era episodes.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Backed the motion and said a mere apology was not enough; called for the broadcaster's head to resign.
Raised a point of order objecting to theft allegations against the Foreign Ministry made without proof.
Raised a point objecting to remarks about cutting the hands of MDP members, saying PNC members are in the same position.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Raised a point of order that calling fellow members 'bot' members breaks Majlis rules and asked the chair to take note.
Presented the compensation report: the committee found the payments conflicted with the Constitution and recommended referral to the Prosecutor General.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Said the live-feed fault had a technical explanation and described the motion as politically motivated.
Criticised the mover's tone and questioned MDP members' conduct on religious matters.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Backed both parts of the motion: the altered verse and state media not giving the opposition airtime; asked for an investigation.
Raised a point that the President spoke of rules not the law and that changes to the law had since been made.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Defended the committee's audit work, saying MDP members first opposed it and that the sub-committee he leads meets weekly.
Said the report shows compensation of islands and lagoons and over MVR 2 billion, and called for quick police and Prosecutor General investigation.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Argued the settlement committee had no legal basis, citing article 268 of the Constitution, and called the payments theft.
Said he wanted to voice concern, backed the report and urged faster investigations.

speakers.name: Hussain Riza Adam
positions: Said the broadcaster had already explained the fault, urged that claims be verified, and called the motion politically driven.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Said earlier urgent matters on religion were ignored in the previous Majlis and accused MDP members of misleading the public.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Urged members not to politicise the Quran and said the opposition should raise such matters responsibly.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Said the opposition had been denied floor time in the previous term and cited earlier MDP members' statements on Quranic punishments.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: As a committee member, noted gaps in audits and spending on repairing the Sri Lanka embassy buildings, and said a recommendation was added.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Said the committee consulted stakeholders and added a 20 percent option, and expected the bill to help reserves and the economy.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Raised a point that the President spoke only about regulations and that laws are made by the Majlis, not by his statements.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said misuse of state funds should be investigated but called the matter political, citing constitutional articles and cabinet and AG sign-off.

speakers.name: Ali Fazad
positions: Presented the Economic Committee report recommending Dhaha Shuaib for the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority board.

decisions: The Speaker announced this was the last sitting of the session and the House would work through the agenda.
Minutes of the 56th and 57th sittings of 2024 were accepted.
The Judiciary Committee was given until 28 February 2025 on the bill amending the Drugs Act.
Kendhoo member Mauroof Zakir's urgent matter was allowed for debate (70 yes, 0 no).
The President's Broadcasting Commission nominees were referred to the Independent Institutions Committee.
The President's Elections Commission nominees were referred to the Independent Institutions Committee.
Debate on the Vice President's Office Bill closed, with the vote left for the day's voting time.
The House broke from 11:55 to 13:01; the Speaker offered condolences to Nolhivaram member Mohamed Rasheed on the death of his wife.
Finance Committee report on Foreign Affairs audits 2010 to 2021 passed 67-0.
Finance Committee report on Higher Education audits 2018 to 2021 passed 67-0.
Finance Committee report on state compensation payments passed 55-11.
Vice President's Office Bill accepted 65-0 and sent to the Judiciary Committee.
Dhaha Shuaib approved for the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority board 69-0.
Chair closed the final sitting of the session, noting 73.3 percent of items before the Majlis were completed this term.
Nominee Shuaib for Maldives Inland Revenue Authority Board member received 69 yes votes, 0 no, 0 abstentions (74 present, 73 eligible; the Speaker has no voting right).
